inference_depth_review: CONFIRMED deep, no change. Step 1 set deep provisionally; the corpus vindicates it. The load-bearing questions are underdetermined by clearly-published sources: the two highest-value primaries are bot-walled, the Indonesian national figure has no published methodology, no platform discloses creator-level distributions, and the best attrition evidence may not exist at all. Shim files unchanged.

loci.name: living-wage-share-magnitude
loci.one_line: Survey and telemetry evidence disagree by two to three orders of magnitude on what share of creators earns a living wage; establish which figure the report prints and why.
loci.rationale: This is the query's central deliverable and the corpus's widest gap: 4-63% (self-selected surveys) against 0.04-1.6% (complete transaction records, platform-disclosed payouts, government-commissioned study). Part of the gap is denominator choice, but Hua et al. measured sampling-frame inflation at only about 10x, leaving a genuine residual. The report cannot print a single share figure without resolving how much of the gap is scope and how much is bias. Depth targets: the two still-blocked primaries (WSJ Twitch leak analysis, Rieder full monetization-linking paper) and the published UK IPO microdata, which permits computing a true median rather than banded percentages.

loci.name: quit-driver-money-vs-motivation
loci.one_line: Self-reported burnout surveys blame financial insecurity; the only two studies that statistically model continuation find income does not predict exit at all.
loci.rationale: The sharpest genuine fight in the corpus, and it maps directly onto required heading 4. Censuswide/BDB (n=1,000) ranks financial instability first by severity at 55% and Ivors/MU (n=311) reports 43% took outside work; against this, Torhonen (n=377) finds intrinsic motivation predicts continuation at p=0.000 while income fails at p=0.052, and the Zhao Cox model (n=1,923) finds affiliation significant but hours streamed not. The two sides measure different constructs - stated reasons among survivors versus modelled predictors of actual exit - and both are routinely reported as why creators quit. The analyst-B exit-survey absence is folded in here because it is the REASON the fight cannot be settled: no instrument in the corpus samples people who already left. Depth target includes a hard search for any true ex-creator exit survey, with the absence documented if none exists.

loci.name: sea-evidence-provenance-and-breadth
loci.one_line: Establish what quantitative creator evidence exists for Southeast Asia beyond Indonesia, and finish tracing the one national-scale figure to a primary record.
loci.rationale: Required heading 5 depends entirely on this. Analyst B verified by tag search that the 146-note corpus holds 14 Indonesia-tagged notes, 2 Philippines-tagged, and ZERO tagged Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia or Singapore - against a decomposition requiring full-ASEAN scope. Meanwhile the single national-scale figure (8 million creators, 63% above UMR) has been traced to TikTok own DPR Komisi I testimony rather than to government statistics, and the BPS press release and DPR hearing record that would confirm it are both bot-walled. Depth work must either recover those primaries or state the absence with precision. Searching in Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai and Tagalog is in scope.

loci.name: attrition-telemetry-absence
loci.one_line: Verify whether any platform-scale creator survival telemetry exists, and adjudicate the one source claiming it.
loci.rationale: Required heading 1 rests on four measurements and one unverified marketing claim. Three targeted OpenAlex sweeps in step 2 returned no platform-scale cohort survival study; if that holds, how many stop and how soon has no good answer and the report must say so with the search documented. The single source asserting otherwise - the creatormap.io claimed 97,601-channel study reporting 46.1% dark and a median lifespan of 8.8 years - must be adjudicated: either it discloses a methodology and becomes the report best attrition figure, or it is an SEO artefact with invented precision and must be named as such. A fresh search angle (non-English literature on Bilibili, Douyin, AfreecaTV, Niconico) is worth one pass before declaring the absence.

loci.name: time-to-income-reframe-tenure-vs-output
loci.one_line: Advice sources give 3-18 month monetization timelines; a 36-million-channel census finds days-active is constant across success tiers and only output volume differs.
loci.rationale: Required heading 3 currently has an answer the evidence does not support. Rieder et al. 2020 (n=36,336,861) state that the average number of days active is surprisingly constant between tiers while elite channels average 940 videos against 294 - so elapsed time is not the operative variable, and the sub-question needs reframing rather than a number of months. Compounding this, vidIQ finds 89% of channels AT the 1,000-subscriber gate have under 5,000 monthly views, so eligibility does not equal income. Small budget because the direction is already clear; the depth work is confirming whether the tenure finding replicates beyond YouTube.

loci.name: unit-of-analysis-and-comparability
loci.one_line: Determine whether a like-for-like cross-platform comparison table is constructable at all, given that every source uses a different unit, denominator, window and currency.
loci.rationale: The query demands every figure carry sample size, year, platform and country - which is table-shaped - but the corpus mixes person-level (BLS, surveys), channel-level (Rieder), campaign-level (Regner) and account-level (Twitch leak) units across incompatible windows, and several headline statistics silently switch between them. This locus decides the report central presentational device: one comparison table, or a table plus an explicit non-comparability crosswalk. The analyst-A BLS/NEA/ACS administrative vein is folded in here as the table ground-truth anchor row - it is the only nationally-representative, self-employment-inclusive earnings series in the corpus (NEA/ACS 2023: full-time artists $70,170 versus part-time $20,380, the latter statistically indistinguishable from all part-time workers at $19,330).

skip_loci.reason: High decision_relevance in the contradiction graph, but the evidence_quality_delta already fully resolves it as definitional/genealogical rather than a measurement dispute needing more data: Goldman's figure is traced backwards through Zippia to a SignalFire VC blog post with no re-measurement possible, and Linktree's 200M is an admitted desk exercise. Further source-gathering will not produce a better denominator; the finding is the audited genealogy itself, which the corpus already has. Folded partial value into the bls-nea-administrative-benchmark locus, which chases a genuinely more rigorous denominator candidate instead.

decision_relevance is medium, not high, and the graph's own evidence_quality_delta concludes the apparent conflict is 'largely scoped differently rather than contradictory' (within-elite churn vs whole-population dispersion can both be true simultaneously) — already resolved, not a genuine open fight requiring depth investigation.

decision_relevance is medium, and the graph's evidence_quality_delta calls Side B 'an analytical correction rather than a competing measurement, and it is correct' with all three major platforms already confirmed to withhold the needed denominator. This is a stable finding to state in the draft, not a further-investigation target — no plausible additional source would unlock the missing per-creator distribution platforms have chosen not to disclose.

The redundancy audit already establishes that the leak's denominator is quoted six incompatible ways and the observation window five incompatible ways, concluding 'pooling them produces nonsense' — this is an audited methodological instability to state, not a number to resolve with more sources, since the underlying leaked dataset itself is internally inconsistent per Dexerto's own analysis.

My angle guidance directs me toward parts the corpus answers worst rather than argues about most, so I leave this for analyst A / direct promotion by the orchestrator rather than duplicating it.

Also a fully-structured, high-relevance step-3 cluster (financial-attribution surveys vs statistically-modelled continuation predictors) with its own opposing_positions already written. Strong candidate, but per angle guidance I am prioritising the exit-survey-absence locus instead, which targets a gap this cluster does not resolve: both sides in the existing cluster sample only currently-active creators, so neither side can speak to actual quitters. That gap is the more load-bearing depth target.

Real definitional dispute (step-3 cluster), but resolving it would not change any share statistic's numerator, only its denominator's label, and the corpus has already traced the Goldman/Zippia/SignalFire provenance chain fully. Diminishing marginal value for report quality relative to the SEA and unit-of-analysis gaps; leaving to analyst A or orchestrator judgment.

Already fully traced by the width sweep (coverage-gaps.md and contradiction-graph.json cluster 'indonesia-63-percent'): origin is TikTok's DPR testimony, not a national statistic; BPS has no content-creator count; the 14% figure is an unrelated Linktree-derived quantity. Re-investigating would waste depth budget on a question the corpus has already settled with primary-source tracing.

Considered proposing a locus to search Chinese/Korean/Japanese-language academic literature (Bilibili, Douyin, Afreeca) for platform-scale survival telemetry the three OpenAlex sweeps missed. Rejected in favor of keeping loci focused on my assigned angle (SEA/time-to-income/unit-of-analysis); attrition-rate-and-timing is also a top-ranked step-3 contradiction cluster likely to be picked by the sibling analyst, and adding a sixth near-duplicate-domain locus would crowd out the SEA-breadth and TikTok-distribution gaps that are currently unclaimed by anyone.
